title: Base change of the tower trace and normalization of the diagonal scalars
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Put $B_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ and $A_T=((B_n)_T)_n$, with quotient transitions, for schemes $T$ over $S$. Use the coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] and their ordinary derived categories [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Let $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be comparison, and let $\mathscr C^+(T)$ be the full subcategory of $D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ whose every level has an etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], meaning it is isomorphic to $\nu_T^*L_n$ for some $L_n\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},B_n)$. Put $P=\mathbf P^1_S$, $W=P\times_SP$, $q:P\to S$, $p_1,p_2:W\to P$, and let $\Delta:P\hookrightarrow W$ be the diagonal [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Use the Tate twist, supported diagonal map $\delta_\bullet:\Delta_*A_P\to A_W(1)[2]$, and splitting traces $t_q,t_1,t_2$ of [det-sp-tower-classes]; here $t_i$ is the trace for $p_i$. Write $F=Rq_{*,\bullet}$ and $G=q_\bullet^*(-)(1)[2]$.
Under the canonical proper exchange and twist identifications for the Cartesian square with edges $p_1,p_2$ over $q,q$, the splitting trace $t_i$ is the pullback of $t_q$ for each $i=1,2$: the unit-and-hyperplane-Chern splitting itself, its inverse, and its second projection commute with this base change as actual tower morphisms.
Let $\alpha_i:A_P\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{i*,\bullet}\Delta_*A_P$ be the canonical direct-image composition identification for $p_i\Delta=1_P$, and define
$$c_i=t_i\circ Rp_{i*,\bullet}(\delta_\bullet)\circ\alpha_i\in\operatorname{End}_{D(\operatorname{Tow}(P,\mathcal O_E))}(A_P[0]).$$
Then $c_1=c_2=1_{A_P}$. More precisely their level-$n$ evaluations, under the canonical direct-image and composition comparisons [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], are $\nu_P^*$ of the ordinary etale finite composites
$$t_{P,B_n}\circ Rp_{i*,B_n}(\delta_{B_n})\circ\alpha_{i,B_n}=1_{(B_n)_P}$$
of [lem-sp-tower-p1-arbitrary-base-integrals], with $N=\ell^n$ and the supported sign convention $\delta_{B_n}u_\Delta=c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$. Both $c_i$ lie in the image of the fully faithful degree-zero embedding of the abelian tower category [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]; consequently equality of their evaluations is equality of these tower-sheaf endomorphisms. No faithfulness of evaluation on arbitrary derived morphisms is asserted. All assertions hold over arbitrary $S$, without a Noetherian or finite-type assumption.

proof.text: Construct k and its forward splitting square and canonical alpha isomorphisms by the normalized splitting base-change lemma.
Use the finite comparison lemma to obtain the Cartier proof and all positive-level finite normalizations for this same k.

The source comparison is the functorial biproduct comparison followed by the biproduct of the shifted line and coefficient isomorphisms. Cancel the mapped splitting isomorphism in the forward square to get inverse base change and exchange invertibility. Postcompose with the second projection, use biprod.lift_snd and traceQ, and functoriality gives trace base change.

Compose each finite WordComparison square with finite_identity and cancel its invertible endpoint comparison to get identity after derived evaluation. Full faithfulness of singleFunctor at degree zero gives unique abelian lifts. Exact evaluation commutes with singleFunctor by its natural isomorphism, so finite singleFunctor faithfulness gives equality of evaluated abelian lifts.

Tower evaluation is sectionwise restriction to (n,U). Extensionality for module-sheaf maps gives equality of the abelian lifts. Apply singleFunctor to recover the scalar identities; the same sectionwise argument proves the restricted equality detection field.
